title: Adaptive per-region trip thresholds and safe fallback orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an adaptive circuit-breaker orchestration that sets per-region, per-dependency, per-model, and per-tenant trip thresholds tied to SLOs and safe fallback behaviors. Aim: reduce blast radius during regional spikes, maintain SLOs for high-value tenants, and provide clear, auditable fallbacks to lower-capacity models or cached results rather than hard failures.
background: We observe frequent transient spikes (region-specific) where backend dependencies (model serving pools, KV cache, feature stores) hit resource pressure. Current global trip thresholds either trigger too early (affecting healthy regions) or too late (causing outages). Previous tickets focused on tenant-aware breakers and probabilistic degradation but lack a unified orchestrator that ties thresholds to live SLO telemetry and enforces safe fallbacks with tenant-priority weighting.
proposed_solution: Introduce a region-aware Circuit Orchestrator service that synthesizes telemetry (p99 latency, p95 error rate, GPU util, queue depth) with tenant SLO metadata to compute dynamic trip points. When a trip occurs, the orchestrator applies a staged fallback policy: 1) local prefix KV cache and route to warm cache; 2) downgrade to pre-validated model variant (e.g., 8-bit quantized or smaller context length) with explicit quality tag; 3) redirect a portion of traffic to dedicated capacity or alternate region depending on tenant priority and cross-region latency budget; 4) as last resort, shed low-priority requests with graceful 429/503 responses including Retry-After and structured diagnostics for callers.
design_decisions: Threshold sources: combine absolute fixed caps (emergency limits) + adaptive baselines (historical p99 moving window) + safety margins from tenant SLOs
Hysteresis: two-window model (short: 30s, long: 5m) with weighted decay to prevent flapping
Decision axis: evaluate signals per (region, dependency, model, tenant) and compute a composite risk score; break triggers when score > configured target for tenant's SLO band
Fallback ordering: cache -> quantized model -> alternate region/dedicated -> shed; order chosen to minimize quality regression and cost impact
Canary rollouts: support gradual percentage ramp for any new fallback rule (0% -> 100%) with auto-rollback on key regressions
Observability: all trip decisions must emit deterministic decision traces and causal links to the signals that triggered the trip
API contract: fallback responses must include structured metadata (fallback_reason, fallback_variant, original_model_id, approximate: true/false) to aid caller resilience
Tenant priority: high-priority tenants (contracted SLAs) get preferential routing to dedicated capacity for short windows before shedding lower-priority tenants
Safety: Emergency global kill-switch and manual override via Console to pause automated fallbacks for audits or incidents
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): implement orchestrator simulation harness and run replay of last 90 days of telemetry to validate thresholds
Phase 1 (canary 5% region traffic): enable orchestrator in passive mode (decisions logged, not enforced) for 48h
Phase 2 (active canary 1 region 5% traffic): enforce fallbacks with detailed monitoring; observe for 72h
Phase 3 (staggered expansion): expand to 3 regions and 25% traffic over 1 week, enable tenant-priority routing for top 10 enterprise tenants
Phase 4 (full): enable across all regions with auto-scaling of orchestrator control-plane and operator runbook enabled
test_plan: Unit tests for decision logic and score calculation (edge cases: missing signals, NaNs)
Integration tests: start/stop synthetic spike generators for GPU/queue depth and verify fallback order and no double-fallback loops
Chaos tests: simulate region partition and ensure orchestrator routes according to policy and honors cross-region latency budget
Load tests: validate hysteresis prevents flip-flopping under oscillatory load patterns
Service-level tests: synthetic tenant SLO regressions to assert high-priority routing works and low-priority shedding respects rate quotas
E2E validation: test clients receive structured fallback metadata and Retry-After headers where applicable
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-region composite risk score, active fallbacks by type, tenant-impact heatmap
SLO alerts: when a tenant's effective SLO breach probability > 5% for 10m, page on-call
Operational alerts: orchestrator decision rate anomalies, failed fallback executions (e.g., model variant missing), and cross-region routing failures
Audit logs: store decision traces for 30 days (queryable by incident responders and compliance teams)
Synthetic guard: automatic rollback when quality regressions (measured via eval-set tokens) exceed configured thresholds during canary
rollback_plan: Immediate automated rollback on detected quality regressions or unacceptable error budgets. Manual rollback via Console if automated path failed. Post-rollback: run root-cause analysis and revert configuration change; if binary (code) release caused failure, tag and roll back deployment per standard release playbook.
